reason: Both correctly explained E:15 as the anti-flood float tripping, told the homeowner to isolate power and water, ruled out foam, and ended with the right escalation to an engineer or Bosch service without naming a definite part. Conversation 1 adapted far better to the integrated-unit constraint, giving a realistic way to dry the tray from the front, a structured way to note when and where water appears so the engineer's diagnosis is faster, and useful cost advice (Bosch fixed-price repair, appliance cover). Conversation 2 was honest and safe but thin: its first instruction ('pull it out slightly') was unusable, and it offered little beyond 'check the seal and hoses, then call an engineer'. Conversation 1 loses some credit for the initial tilt advice and for nudging the homeowner towards running test cycles and sliding the unit out themselves, which is why the margin is only slight.
